title: [3.0-beta6] Initiating bolus when connection counter is already running causes time-out
body:
Issue happened using the Dash pod.
Sometimes the bluetooth connection timer is already running when issuing a bolus command.
When that happens, the system cannot connect any more to the Dash pod and you have to wait until time-out before the system responds again. So it looks neither the origingal task nor the bolus is executed until after the time-out and a new retry.
I have attached the relevant log files.
The time the problem happens is 13:49:32:610
[AndroidAPS._2021-11-20_00-00-04_.1.zip](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/files/7594855/AndroidAPS._2021-11-20_00-00-04_.1.zip)
.

comments.body:
I don't understand what is the bug here.
After reading the logs, it looks like a bolus command timed out on connect. 
Connections can fail from time to time, if this happens often mark your phone model as 'not supported'.

It is indeed no serieus problem. It happens only very occasionally. What puzzles me in the persistant impossibility to connect. Usually when I see a connection problem bringing the phone close to the Dash pod solves the problem, but when this happens it really refuses to connect and runs to time-out.
It does not seem phone related, I experienced this behavior with three different phones, roughly once per one or two Dash pods.
So, in practice not a problem, but puzzling.
Yes, I also don't know why this happens sometimes.

I don't think this is a bug.
The fact that you initiate a bolus where there is a pending connection it doesn't make the connection to timeout.
It would timeout anyway.

As said, it is not a problem in practice. But maybe good to consider to have a message in the final version when this happens, else the user does not understand why it is not connecting. Or will the connection counter remain visible, also in the non-developer versions? (I personally like this additional info to understand what is happening).
Yes, the connection counter will remain visible.
